name: St. Stephen Apartments
headline: St. Stephen Apartments (St. Stephen Senior Apartments) is a 50-home, all income-restricted building for adults 62+ in Denver's Central Park neighborhood, built by MGL Partners on land ground-leased from St. Stephen Missionary Baptist Church with a 2022 Round One federal 9% award; it opened in summer 2025.
why_it_matters: It is a finished faith-land deal: a long, low-cost church ground lease that pays the congregation an annuity and passes the church's property tax exemption through to the project by making the church a general partner.

status.label: Built and fully leased (grand opening 2025-09-11)
status.detail: Groundbreaking was 2023-11-14; first residents moved in in summer 2025 and the grand opening on 2025-09-11 reported the building fully leased. Another 2026 CHFA application lists it as opened in August 2025. No placed-in-service or 8609 record was found online.

next_step: Watch for CHFA compliance or placed-in-service records and confirm the source and amount of the state credits the opening release mentions.

key_numbers.meaning: About $12.6M over 10 years; the 2022 award report shows no state credit.
5 homes at 30% AMI, 12 at 40%, 18 at 50% and 15 at 60%.

facts.value: 0.6-acre portion of the church's land in a Difficult Development Area, zoned R-MU-20 (multifamily by right); new zone lot created by a ZLAM filed January 2022
Four stories, two elevators, 19 surface spaces plus shared church parking; hydronic heating, all-electric ready, solar-ready; NGBS Bronze
Santulan Architecture, BC Builders (GC), Silva Management Partners (on-site management)

money.note: Application put equity at $11,298,504; Wells Fargo was the equity investor and construction lender.
The opening releases say state credits allocated by CHFA were used; the 2022 Round One report shows none.

parties.role: Landowner / ground lessor; administrative general partner
parties.name: St. Stephen Missionary Baptist Church

background.text: The church and MGL signed an MOU in 2021 and a land lease in early 2022; the church keeps the new zone lot and leases it into the tax-credit partnership, giving the historically African American congregation (in Denver since 1900, at this site since 2015) a steady income.
The church becomes an administrative general partner so its property tax exemption flows through to the project; it also provides vehicle access easements and shared parking.
Residents get RTD NECO passes (budgeted for one year) and access to the church's food bank and van transport.

The market study's capture rates (63.4% overall; 76.1% at 50% AMI and 74% at 60%) were well above CHFA guidelines; the application cited 100% occupancy and waiting lists at the market area's 800 senior tax-credit units.
At award, MGL slated financial close for May 2023 and completion by summer 2024; construction instead began in November 2023 and finished in summer 2025.
At the groundbreaking the partners listed CHFA, Wells Fargo, Impact Development Fund, the Colorado Division of Housing, the City and County of Denver and Brookfield Residential as funders.

timeline.event: Church and MGL sign an MOU
Zone lot amendment filed with Denver; land lease executed in early 2022
CHFA Round One award report lists $1,255,389 federal 9% credit
MGL announces the award; closing targeted for May 2023
Opened (as listed in a 2026 CHFA application by another developer)

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award report gives the address as 2050 N. Uinta, while the opening releases give 2189 N Valentia Street.
The application says the congregation voted to lease the land for the next 50 years, while the groundbreaking and opening releases describe a 65-year land lease.
The 2022 Round One award report shows only federal 9% credit for this deal, while the opening releases say it was financed with federal and state tax credits allocated by CHFA.
The application budgeted $17,555,622, while the opening releases give a $19.6 million development.
